sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.
This is the second bail application.

By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.1067 of 2023 at Police Station-Tajganj, District-Agra under Sections 376, 120B I.P.C. and Section 4/17 of the POCSO Act and Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.
The applicant is in jail since 15.12.2023.

sentences.text: The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court on 09.04.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Hare Krishna Tripathi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1.
The applicant has been falsely implicated in this case by an NGO which is habitual of falsely implicating persons.
2. On 23.08.2019 the said NGO had filed an F.I.R. in respect of the same victim.
The age of the victim at that point in time was depicted as 16 years in the statement of the victim recorded in the year 2019.
In the present case, the F.I.R. was got registered on 14.12.2023.
It is alleged that the victim is 17 years of age.
The age of the victim is contradicted by the aforesaid documents.
3. Clearly the victim is being used by some interested persons to blackmail innocent persons like the applicant.
This fact could not be brought to the notice of this Court on the earlier occasion.
4. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated in the investigation and has joined the trial proceedings.
The applicant never tampered with the evidence nor did he influence any witness.
5. The applicant never adopted any dilatory tactics or impeded the process of the trial.

6. The Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.31630 of 2024 (Balbeer Rathoure v.State of U.P. and 3 others) in the instant criminal case records that the status report sent by the trial court records that the prosecution proposes to examine 9 witnesses to bring home the charges.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.31630 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: Balbeer Rathoure v.State of U.P. and 3 others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, not a single witness has been examined till date.

The status report sent by the trial court also records that the victim as well as the other prosecution witnesses are not appearing before the learned trial court on the appointed dates despite issuance of summons.
7.
Prosecution witnesses are delaying the trial only to prolong the incarceration of the applicant.

8. The applicant claims congruency in role and seeks parity in relief granted to the co-accused-Balbeer Rathoure who has been enlarged on bail by this Court by order dated 26.09.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.31630 of 2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.31630 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 9. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.

sentences.text: The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of the applicant influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Dugar Singh @ Bhola be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
